episode_title: UYB 124: Why Great Ideas Never Get Finished — with Shauna VanderHoek

real_qa.q: What is the first step Shauna VanderHoek recommends when evaluating an unfinished project?
real_qa.r: The first thing is to ask why you are doing the project. Many times it's easy to get started because you think it's a good idea, but you might decide you have more important things to do. Make sure you want to move forward with the project and that it's worth doing before investing time on finishing it.

real_qa.q: What are the main reasons great ideas and projects stall according to business operations strategy?
real_qa.r: Projects stall due to competing priorities, biting off more than you can chew at once, unrealistic expectations, and not having the right team or resources. Sometimes you're trying to do too much on your own or with too small a team and need to bring in outside resources.
real_qa.requete: why do projects stall competing priorities

real_qa.q: What project management tools does Shauna VanderHoek recommend for small businesses without a full-time project manager?
real_qa.r: For micro businesses, Trello is a great tool because it helps keep track of communications between team members about specific tasks. If teams are already familiar with Excel, they can structure it as a project management tool with different tabs. Other options include Monday, Smartsheets, and Microsoft Project.
real_qa.requete: best project management tools small business

real_qa.q: How should founders communicate project purpose to prevent team momentum loss mid-project?
real_qa.r: It's critical to let the team know why you're doing something and the bigger picture of what it will do for the company. Unless they understand the why, they won't have interest in reaching the result. People need to feel part of something that's growing, not just doing drudgery. Getting them back on the mission and vision when momentum flags helps teams re-engage.
real_qa.requete: how to keep team motivated during long projects

real_qa.q: What action can entrepreneurs take this week to restart an important stalled project?
real_qa.r: Step back and decide what components need to happen and in what order. Create a good project plan by identifying which domino must go first, because unless you get that first domino going, you're not ever going to get the last one done.

guest.bio_context: Shauna has worked in project management and operations streamlining for over 30 years, starting at age 15. She spent her career designing systems and improving workflows for Fortune 100 companies, and now focuses on helping small business owners by mapping projects, building templates, and mentoring project managers so progress doesn't depend solely on the founder.
